name: issue_1066_mixed_day_heat_then_cool_then_heat
description: A mild day that starts cold, warms past the ceiling and cools again by evening (the 'mixed day' from docs/08 section 6f). Band 68F/74F, arming margin 2F. The thermostat must follow the nearest edge: heat from the cold morning through 71F, flip to cool at 72F, stay cool through 73-75F and the 71F evening gap, and flip back to heat only at 70F. The commanded mode changes exactly three times across the day (cool -> heat, heat -> cool, cool -> heat).
source: Issue #1066 plan, Design D 'mixed day' worked example (docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f)
notes: Occupant impact: the house is heated while it is cold, cooled when it overheats, and heated again as the evening cools, without ever running the wrong system and without chatter in between.

Three genuine mode changes from the initial cool: 06:30 heat (breach), 10:30 cool (indoor 72), 19:00 heat (indoor 70). Each is asserted as a comfort_family_switch event carrying the exact indoor reading. The switch event is emitted only on a genuine change, and the in-between readings (09:30 and 18:00 at 71F, inside the gap) are the ones that would produce extra changes if hysteresis broke; the final-state and never-cool-after-19:00 assertions catch that. The harness has no 'count of mode changes' assertion type, so an exact count is additionally covered by tests/test_nearest_edge_arming.py.

(a) Scenario effectiveness: on origin/main a mild day is natively cooling; heat needed a floor breach beyond the mild deadband, a recency check and a 90 s sustain, and the revert to cool needed a recovery margin plus sustain. The 19:00 heat arm at 70F (no breach: 70 > 68) cannot occur on the old design, and the 06:30 switch would not complete at the first reading, so the comfort_family_switch assertions and the final comfort_family=heating would fail.
(b) Docs vs production: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f 'Mixed day, floor 68 F, ceiling 74 F, m = 2 F' table (06:30, 10:30, 14:00, 18:00 rows).

(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: the evening cools below the floor with the AC still armed, or the morning sun overheats the house while the furnace is armed, for the length of a multi-step confirmation sequence.
Classification fields: day_type=mild, hvac_mode=off, windows_recommended=true with the classifier's 10:00/17:00 window times (classifier.py DAY_TYPE_MILD).

assertions.reason: Indoor 66F is below the 68F floor: heat is armed on the first reading (breach).
Indoor reaches ceiling-m = 72F: the thermostat flips to cool/74 at the boundary, not after waiting for a breach. The 09:30 reading of 71F (inside the gap) left it in heat.
The cool flip is a real command: a comfort band is sent in cool mode on the ceiling edge (74F) at 10:30.
Evening: indoor falls to floor+m = 70F and heat is armed before the floor is reached. The 18:00 reading of 71F (gap) had kept cool.
Final family is heating after the third change.
Final commanded mode is heat at comfort_heat.
After the 19:00 heat arm, cool is never commanded again (no flap at the 69F reading).

verdict.summary: On a mixed day the thermostat is armed on the nearest edge at every step: heat in the cold morning, cool from 72F, heat again from 70F in the evening.
verdict.observed_behavior: Three genuine mode changes at 66F (breach), 72F and 70F; readings of 71F in the gap leave the mode untouched.
